speaker: Town Crier
text: Hear ye, hear ye! Three thousand miles of sea between 'em!

speaker: Town Crier
text: In the East, the King. In the West, the General.

speaker: Town Crier
text: Two Georges. One continent. Let's go!

speaker: King George III
text: Kneel, colonial. The Crown would like a word:

speaker: King George III
text: you're George the First of Nothing. I'm George the Third.

speaker: King George III
text: You didn't make your fortune, boy, you married it.

speaker: King George III
text: Martha had the acres. You were just tall enough to carry it.

speaker: King George III
text: Twenty-two, one volley in the woods lit war across my empire.

speaker: King George III
text: Father of your country? Please. You're the father of a fire.

speaker: King George III
text: Then it poured on Fort Necessity, your powder soaking wet.

speaker: King George III
text: That's the closest thing to a reign you're ever gonna get.

speaker: King George III
text: You marched out on the Fourth of July. Look it up, boy:

speaker: King George III
text: your first Independence Day? A white flag. Enjoy.

speaker: King George III
text: I paid for the war you started, sent a Stamp, you called it poison.

speaker: King George III
text: That's not tyranny, colonial. That's an invoice.

speaker: King George III
text: You begged to wear my redcoat. Wrote letters, pled and pined.

speaker: King George III
text: Loudoun left you on read. Commission: declined.

speaker: King George III
text: You're not a rebel, George. You're a reject with a gun.

speaker: King George III
text: I'm the Crown. You're the help that got ideas. Kneel. I'm done.

speaker: George Washington
text: You done?

speaker: George Washington
text: Four balls through my coat on the Monongahela,

speaker: George Washington
text: two horses shot from under me, and I'm still here to tell ya:

speaker: George Washington
text: Farmer George, you spread manure, but you can't make me sweat.

speaker: George Washington
text: You're all powder and no ball. I haven't felt it yet.

speaker: George Washington
text: Sure, I lost the Fourth of July in fifty-four. It's true.

speaker: George Washington
text: Now the whole world spends the Fourth celebrating losing you.

speaker: George Washington
text: "Left on read"? We sent the Olive Branch, on our knees, to plead.

speaker: George Washington
text: You wouldn't even take it. You left a whole continent on read.

speaker: George Washington
text: You rented Hessians. I crossed the ice and hit 'em at eight a.m.

speaker: George Washington
text: Boxing Day in Trenton? I boxed up nine hundred of 'em.

speaker: George Washington
text: You never came to fight yourself, so we melted down your statue:

speaker: George Washington
text: forty-two thousand bullets, George. We fired you back at you.

speaker: George Washington
text: You wanted quarters in our houses? Here's a quarter from my hand.

speaker: George Washington
text: That's my face on it, George. I'm the currency of this land.

speaker: King George III
text: "Currency"? Your money crashed so hard it's a phrase:

speaker: King George III
text: "not worth a Continental." My forgers printed it for days.

speaker: King George III
text: And your record, General? The fort that had your name on it

speaker: King George III
text: surrendered twenty-eight hundred men by teatime. Own it.

speaker: King George III
text: Your favorite, Benedict Arnold, flipped his coat to red.

speaker: King George III
text: Your best general saw us both and picked the other George instead.

speaker: King George III
text: The cherry tree? A parson made it up to sell a book.

speaker: King George III
text: The one story of you not lying? It's a lie. Go look.

speaker: King George III
text: I reigned for sixty years. You did eight, then ran home to the plow.

speaker: King George III
text: Couldn't hold a crown, so you called quitting "noble." Take a bow.

speaker: King George III
text: And spare me "liberty." Your man Harry ran to me and sailed off free,

speaker: King George III
text: while you begged to get back your "property."

speaker: King George III
text: Your teeth ain't wood, that's folklore. It's hippo ivory beneath,

speaker: King George III
text: and nine you bought from people that you owned,

speaker: King George III
text: so every time you said "freedom," George, you said it with their teeth.

speaker: George Washington
text: You wanna talk chains? Your ships hauled more than any flag at sea.

speaker: George Washington
text: Liverpool got rich while you stirred slave-grown sugar in your tea.

speaker: George Washington
text: My will freed mine. Your empire kept its chains after you were dead,

speaker: George Washington
text: so don't you preach me freedom with a crown upon your head.

speaker: George Washington
text: I lost more battles than I won? Correct. I still won the war.

speaker: George Washington
text: You won the fights and lost a continent. What were you fighting for?

speaker: George Washington
text: The cherry tree's a myth? Fine. I cannot tell a lie, it's true:

speaker: George Washington
text: I never chopped a cherry tree. I chopped your family tree in two.

speaker: George Washington
text: Then your mind went. You talked for hours till you foamed,

speaker: George Washington
text: so Doctor Willis strapped you in a chair. Your Majesty, enthroned.

speaker: George Washington
text: Your piss ran blue. "Blue blood"? Nah, George. That was your bladder.

speaker: George Washington
text: Herschel found a planet, and he named it "George's Star."

speaker: George Washington
text: The world renamed it Uranus. That's exactly where you are.

speaker: George Washington
text: In '82 you drafted your abdication, tried to give the crown away.

speaker: George Washington
text: Same spring, they offered one to me. "Banish these thoughts." No way.

speaker: George Washington
text: Then the war was won, and you asked your painter what I'd do.

speaker: George Washington
text: West said, "He'll go back to his farm." And you (yes, you)

speaker: George Washington
text: said, "If he does that, he'll be the greatest man in the world."

speaker: George Washington
text: So I handed back my sword.

speaker: George Washington
text: Then I handed back the presidency.

speaker: George Washington
text: Your words, George. Not mine.

speaker: George Washington
text: First thing you ever got right.
